subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should OpenClaw fix this by making CLI health/status/stability RPC-first with read-only/no-maintenance fallback, by enforcing a gateway-owned single-writer lease, or by requiring forensic harness proof before choosing the ownership model?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the permanent fix changes shared-state ownership and recovery semantics for documented operator commands and doctor/migration paths, so automation should not pick the policy boundary alone.

options.title: RPC-first no-maintenance CLI
options.body: Make health/status/stability ask the running gateway first and ensure any active-gateway file fallback opens shared state read-only without journal, checkpoint, or migration side effects.

options.title: Single-writer gateway lease
options.body: Have the gateway own write and WAL-maintenance access, with non-gateway processes failing closed or routing through gateway APIs unless an explicit maintenance mode is active.

options.title: Forensic harness first
options.body: Pause implementation until the reporter's sanitized DB bundle and a native runtime harness prove the exact SQLite helper/runtime interaction before selecting the policy.

recommendation.title: RPC-first no-maintenance CLI
recommendation.body: Make health/status/stability ask the running gateway first and ensure any active-gateway file fallback opens shared state read-only without journal, checkpoint, or migration side effects.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision cuts across the database-first runtime-state architecture and the gateway/CLI ownership boundary introduced through PR 78595.
